- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3142-3148 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]

  WHY: A PR that authors valid-looking but misleading security directives in README.md would have those directives read as trusted context by the reviewer models, since the prompt's injection guard applies to UNTRUSTED-wrapped sections only and this block carries no wrapping.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3147-3148 | severity=NIT | confidence=[5]

  WHY: Log noise and confusion during operator triage; two warnings firing for the same root cause make it harder to identify what actually happened.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3116 | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The workflow warning always prints reason=not_regular_file regardless of the Python helper's actual rejection reason (symlink_path, unsafe_file, file_changed).
  WHY: An operator triaging outcome=omitted for an oversized README sees not_regular_file and must consult helper stderr for the real cause of an oversized-file rejection.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:38-39 | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]

- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:38-39 | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: Production `allowed()` carries a one-off hardcoded filename exclusion (`if name == "tests/test_audit_plans_command.py": return False`). The exclusion is keyed on the exact test filename with no marker, convention, or shared constant.
  WHY: A future rename of `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py` silently desynchronises the production rule from the test in `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:8200,8215` — the assertion would still hold (because the test fixture recreates the file at the literal name), but the production code's real intent ("this test embeds operator-facing command text") would silently transfer the test file's content into the reviewer workspace. The contract is not anchored to any property of the test file (path, marker comment, or naming convention), so a rename has no inherent warning signal.
- Requirement: "Read README.md with no-follow, size-bounded validation, and keep PR content separate from trusted instructions."
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` lines 3125-3157 (the `Pre-assemble static context` step that assembles `pre_assembled_static.txt`); consumer of `pre_assembled_static.txt` is `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh` which inlines it into the editor prompt.
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff adds no-follow reading and size-bounded rejection of symlink/oversize/oversize/oversize/non-regular READMEs (the no-follow and validation half of the requirement), but it concatenates the trimmed regular README content directly into `pre_assembled_static.txt` between the trusted `=== UNATTENDED SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS ===` and `=== AGENTS.MD ===` blocks without any untrusted-content framing. The README section at lines 3142-3146 has the same `=== ... ===` header style as the trusted sections immediately above it, so the model has no signal that the content boundary differs. A regular PR-authored README can therefore inject instructions that the model treats as part of the same trusted prefix that the OpenRouter prompt cache key anchors on. The "keep PR content separate from trusted instructions" half of the requirement has no corresponding diff hunk.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
